_README: THE SCORING MODEL. Edit this file, not the score.
Every item is one concrete deliverable with a WEIGHT in body-of-work units
(roughly: how much of this project's effort it is/was) and a VALUE in 0..1.
A section's score is the weighted mean of its items. The overall score is the
An item's value comes from exactly one of two places, and the difference is
the whole point of this file:
"value": n      -- ATTESTED. A human confirmed it. `evidence` must say how.
"probe": "..."  -- MEASURED. score.py computes it from the tree every run.
⚠ THE ONE RULE: never raise an attested value because something LOOKS done.
Raise it when a run on real hardware confirmed it, and put the run in
`evidence`. This project's most expensive bugs have all been things that
read as working -- see docs/STATE.md, `a stepped-over call still answers`.
⚠ THE BAR IS 'ntvdm SUPERSET ON XP-32', ONE BAR, FOR EVERY SECTION. It is NOT
the DOS games bar. Doom and Skyroads being playable is two items here, not a
score of 85. Scoring the halves against different bars is how the 2026-09-04
review got a headline of 65 that its own components did not support.

_guests_README: THE SHELF. `state` is the ONLY place a guest is credited, and it moves only
on a confirmed run on real hardware. 'launches' is not 'works' -- Paint
launched and drew for four sessions while silently saving to the wrong
directory. Use `partial` for that, and say what is missing.
done    = does the thing the program exists to do, user-confirmed
partial = launches and does some of its job (counts half)
